questions.question: When the amplitude of the driving excitation in a linear resistive medium (resistance $26$ units) is multiplied by $5$, by what factor does the rate of quadratic energy dissipation change?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A physical quantity $f(z)$ increases linearly from $0$ to $54$ units over the interval $z \in [0, 6]$. Evaluate $\int_0^{6} f(z)\,dz$.
questions.solution: Area of the right triangle under the linear curve is $\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 54 = 162$.
questions.explanation: Apply the graphical slope & area integration principles in Atoms & Nuclei (Binding Energy per Nucleon).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An interaction reduces the mechanical energy of a body to $\frac{1}{6}$ of its initial value $E_0 = 204\text{ J}$. How much mechanical energy is lost during the interaction?
questions.solution: Dissipated energy $\Delta E = E_0 - E_0/6 = 204 - 34 = 170\text{ J}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the energy efficiency & dissipation principles in Atoms & Nuclei (Radioactive Decay & Half-Life).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For a mechanical assembly to remain stable, the stiffness parameter $k$ must exceed the critical value $k_c = 35\text{ N/m}$. If the operating stiffness is set to $k = 77\text{ N/m}$, what is the excess stiffness margin $k - k_c$?
questions.solution: The stability margin is $k - k_c = (77) - 35 = 42\text{ N/m}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the critical threshold & equilibrium principles in Atoms & Nuclei (Binding Energy per Nucleon).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The frequency response function $H(\omega) = \frac{74}{\omega + 2^2 / \omega}$ for $\omega > 0$ reaches its maximum value at $\omega = \omega_0$. Determine $\omega_0$ and $H(\omega_0)$.
questions.solution: By AM-GM, $\omega + 2^2/\omega \ge 2(2)$ with equality at $\omega_0 = 2$, giving $H_{\max} = \frac{74}{2\cdot 2} = \frac{37}{2}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the resonance & extremum condition principles in Atoms & Nuclei (Bohr Orbit Radius & Rydberg Spectra).
